panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 3 panels (A, B, C). A: Radiograph of the femur in a 48-year-old woman with Mulibrey nanism; caption explicitly states fibrous dysplasia of the femur with arrows marking the FD areas. Article title and text attribute FD to Mulibrey nanism. Femoral FD is not represented in the provided vocabulary, so it is listed as a proposed finding. B: Radiograph of the tibia in a 13-year-old boy; caption explicitly names tibial fibrous dysplasia, arrow marks the lesion. Tibia was the most common FD site in this Mulibrey nanism cohort (47%), and the article is specifically about the skeletal phenotype of Mulibrey nanism with fibrous dysplasia. C: Radiograph of an extended fibular lesion in a 39-year-old man with Mulibrey nanism; caption states fibrous dysplasia of the fibula with deformity from a previous fracture in FD-weakened bone, arrows marking FD areas. Fibular FD is not in the provided vocabulary, so findings are proposed; a fracture-related deformity in an FD lesion...

in_text_mentions: Radiographic changes corresponding to FD were found in 19/33 patients (58%); changes were monostotic in 58% and polyostotic in 42%. FD was equally frequent in females and males (58% and 57%, respectively). In children, FD was found in 4/6 boys (67%) and 7/11 girls (64%). In adults, FD was observed in 50%. FD lesions were encountered in all long bones but were most often present in the tibia (9/19 patients, 47%) (Figure 3). No lesions were observed in the spine, pelvis, hands or feet, or other bones outside the long bones.

panels.figure_caption: Skeletal features in a 39 years old male patient. The long bones are slender, cortices thick and medullar cavities narrow. (A) In the humerus, cortical thickness is most pronounced distally. Note also the especially broad metaphysis. (B) In the radius and ulna, cortical thickness is most prominent centrally. Note also the slight bowing of the bones. (C) In the femur, cortical thickness is most pronounced proximally. Note the old fracture in mid‐shaft with impaired healing. (D) In the tibia and fibula, cortical thickness is most prominent centrally. Note the areas of irregular cortex indicative of FD in the distal half of both the tibia and fibula. (E) The spine shows signs of mild scoliosis but normal vertebral width. (F) Vertebral bodies are tall with concave endplates. This patient had no history of GH therapy.

in_text_mentions: le. Her parents were relatives, and she was the only person in the family with dwarfism and such disorders. Another finding of note was that the patient’s external genitalia were normal and premature. Ultrasonography of the pelvis showed small ovaries with a few antral follicles and a small uterus. Chest CT scan demonstrated increased pericardial thickness with an abnormal thorax and scoliosis of the vertebral column (Figure 3). CT scan of the abdomen revealed mild hepatomegaly and ascites (Figure 4). In pelvic CT scan, hypoplastic uterus and ovaries were present. The other organs were normal.
